registration.task: 48-b two-reader installment 2 — an independent chain reader LIVING IN qthe that verifies the crab-traps repo's own receipt chains
registration.direction: REVERSED relative to installment 1 (crab-traps 47-b walked 8 fleet chains): now the qthe side reads crab-traps. Zero code shared with the installment-1 walker, fleet-seeds walkers, or crab-traps sources — this reader is written from the stone-v1 law itself (hash-chain of rows; every link is a sha256 over exact bytes; fail closed on any tamper at a precise row index).
registration.target_repo: SuperInstance/crab-traps @ working tree main 37c34bb; each chain additionally pinned to the commit that produced it
registration.reader_module: two_reader/reader.mjs (stdlib-only Node: node:crypto, node:fs, node:path, node:process — zero imports from any other repo)
registration.seal_discipline: THIS file was sealed BEFORE the first official run: seal.self_sha256_masked is the sha256 of these exact bytes with the seal.self_sha256_masked field replaced by 64 '0's (fixed-position mask, byte length unchanged); seal.mtime_local is forced back onto the file with utimes AFTER the last write so the recorded mtime binds the sealed bytes and PREDATES every run receipt in two_reader/run_receipts/. Zero API spend; MOTH_KEY unused (all choices deterministic).

law.fold: h_i = sha256( hex(h_{i-1}) + ':' + bytes_sha256(row_i) + ':' + row_id_i ) over rows in registered order; tip = h_N
law.row_digest: bytes_sha256(row) = sha256 of the file's raw bytes at worker/-relative path inside the crab-traps working tree
law.fail_closed: exit 0 requires: every row file present, every row digest equal to its pin, every check true, tip equal to expect_tip; ANY failure exits non-zero and reports first_failure at a precise chain/row/check
law.chain_shape_honesty: crab-traps does NOT keep stone-v1 parent-link row chains natively. Its receipts form a PRE-REGISTRATION BINDING CHAIN (predictions sealed before any call -> results embedding pre_registration.sha256 -> verdict; receipts bound by byte digests and cross-field bindings). The two-reader enforces the stone-v1 LAW over that shape: the walker's rolling fold turns the row sequence into a real hash chain whose tip pins order AND content, so any single-byte tamper in any row breaks the chain at that row.

claims.text: All 49 rows of the three crab-traps receipt chains (crab45c: 19 rows, crab44a: 4 rows, crab46a: 26 rows) re-hash to their pinned bytes_sha256 from genesis, every registered binding check holds (embedded pre_registration digests, whitening order sha over the actual selected array, permutation 0..95, usage-row-to-call-receipt bindings, verdict content constants), and each chain's rolling fold tip equals its pinned expect_tip (crab45c f3ed1b63…, crab44a 0886f81d…, crab46a 45812cff…).
claims.verdict_rule: PASS iff the official run's reader receipts show ok=true for all three chains with tips equal to the pinned values and zero failed checks; else FAIL naming the first failing row/check

claims.text: Tampering ANY single byte in ANY row of ANY chain is detected fail-closed and localized: the reader exits non-zero with first_failure.row_index equal to the tampered row (every row carries its own bytes pin, so localization is at the tampered row itself, not downstream).
claims.verdict_rule: PASS iff the self-test's full tamper sweep (one byte flipped in each of the 49 rows) yields exit!=0 AND row_index==tampered row for all 49, plus controls: missing row file fails with that row's index, wrong --expect-tip on good bytes fails at tip, tampered usage ROW inside usage.jsonl is detected at the usage row's index; else FAIL naming the escape

claims.text: Verification is byte-identical across two runs: the two official run receipts differ ONLY in the declared run_at wall-clock field; every computed digest, check result, tip and verdict byte is identical.
claims.verdict_rule: PASS iff run1/run2 receipts are byte-equal after normalizing receipt.run_at to a fixed value; else FAIL with the first differing path

claims.text: Absence fails closed: a chain whose row file is missing (or a chain id that does not exist) exits non-zero with a precise error; a wrong expected tip on good bytes also fails closed.
claims.verdict_rule: PASS iff all absence/wrong-tip controls exit non-zero with the failing row or tip named; else FAIL naming the false-accept

claims.text: The reader is code-independent of the installment-1 walker and of all fleet/crab verifier code: two_reader/reader.mjs imports ONLY node: builtins (plus reads registration.json as DATA), shares no code with crab-traps' arena-scenarios-003-two-reader-walker.mjs or fleet-seeds walkers; pins are DATA reused verbatim from the fleet wave-46 rollout where the fleet pinned them, the rest resolved by disclosed reconnaissance.
claims.verdict_rule: PASS iff the static import scan of two_reader/*.mjs shows zero non-node: specifiers outside two_reader/ and zero string references to crab-traps or fleet-seeds code modules; else FAIL with the offending import

registration.pin_resolution_disclosure: Fleet-pinned digests (45c predictions/results, 44a predictions/results, moth fixture ebc8a43d…) are reused VERBATIM from fleet-seeds wave-46 claims.json (cfaf425b…) and re-verified byte-equal against the local crab-traps working tree @ 37c34bb AND against the pinned commits via git blob ids (all stable). All other row digests and the three tips were resolved by pre-registration reconnaissance over the local clone (git blob at pinned commit == working-tree bytes for every row; verified before sealing) and are pinned here BEFORE the official run, exactly the 46-e disclosed-reconnaissance pattern.

reseal_history.reason: pre-run QA smoke (not an official run) caught a row-numbering defect in crab46a: call-01-request was registered with index 3, colliding with order-reuse-receipt, and row 23 was missing (cross-row JSON caches keyed by index mis-bound). Indices are bookkeeping only — NO pin digest, tip, claim, or check changed; tips recomputed and byte-identical (fold is index-independent: h_i = sha256(h_{i-1} ':' digest ':' row_id)). Fixed and re-sealed; seal #2 predates the official runs.

seal.method: masked-self-sha + utimes-restored mtime; verify: replace seal.self_sha256_masked with 64 zeros, sha256 the exact file bytes, compare; stat mtime must equal mtime_local (ms) and predate all run receipts
